## Summary
Reviewed head e5d46f57. Test-only change to packages/server/tests/doctor.test.js. Both hardcoded sites from issue 7815 (the two literal ports) are replaced with OS-assigned ports bound via listen(0) on 127.0.0.1. The free-port case asserts pass; a new held-port case asserts warn. Title, body and commit contain no issue-number hash references, carry Trial-Closes: 7815, and have no attribution.

## Strengths
- Doctor's probe (checkPortAvailable in src/doctor.js) does listen(port, '127.0.0.1'), and the test fixtures bind the identical address. Same IP and port means EADDRINUSE on Linux, macOS and Windows alike, so the held-port warn assertion does not depend on platform or IPv6 behaviour.
- Both directions of the pass/warn branch are now deterministic, which was the issue's preferred design (option 1).
- Listeners are closed in finally (held cases) or immediately (freePort); no handle outlives a test. The file exits cleanly under node --test.
- Verified: the file passes 124/124 with 59123/59124 unheld and with both held by an external process. Mutation (probe always resolves) turns the two new held-port tests red.
- I also mutated the probe to bind 0.0.0.0: the same two tests go red on macOS (BSD semantics let 0.0.0.0 bind alongside a held 127.0.0.1), so the tests genuinely pin the probe address. Source restored from backup with cp afterwards (src/doctor.js identical to the original).

## Critical
None.

## Suggestions
- TOCTOU in freePort (bind 0, close, then doctor probes): a window of microseconds in which another process could take the port. This is the design the issue itself recommends, ephemeral allocation does not immediately reissue a just-freed port on the common OSes, and the exposure is orders of magnitude smaller than a fixed literal. Acceptable; DEFER (only a doctor-side injectable probe would remove it, which is out of scope).
- The companion test 'a bound port is only a warning' asserts passed equals checks.every(status != 'fail'), which re-derives the expectation from the same checks list. If an unrelated check fails on the host, both sides are false and the test no longer pins that a warn does not fail the run. It did go red under the always-resolve mutant here, so it works in a clean environment. Cheap to FOLD: additionally assert the Port row is not the cause, e.g. assert.ok(checks.every(c => c.name === 'Port' || c.status !== 'fail') ? passed : true), or filter out Port and compare. Optional.

## Nitpicks
- The pre-existing 'passed is true when no failures' keeps its if/else shape, so it can silently take the failure branch; unchanged by this PR.
- Observation only (pre-existing, out of scope): the doctor probes 127.0.0.1 while the real server may bind a wider interface, so doctor can report available for a port that start would find taken on another interface.

## Verdict
Approve
